subject: Hosting pathway options and proposed pacing for NimbleOps MAP
messages:
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia@redwood.ai>
To: Daniel Park <daniel@nimbleops.com>
Cc: Priya Sharma <priya@nimbleops.com>
Date: 2027-04-10T09:12:00Z
Subject: Draft MAP: hosting options + timeline (quick read)

Hi Daniel / Priya,

Thanks again for the call this morning — good alignment on business goals and the data residency constraint for EU customers. Per our conversation I’ve attached a short Mutual Action Plan (v1.3) that outlines three deployment pathways (Hosted, Dedicated, Private), the evaluation checkpoints we recommend, and a near-term pacing suggestion to keep the proof-of-value on a 6–8 week runway.

Key highlights in the MAP:
- Hosted API: fastest to production (1–2 weeks) but requires data processing in our EU region (we can route to Frankfurt) and standard data processing addendum.
- Dedicated: reserved GPU pools in your tenancy; better isolation, predictable throughput; suggested evaluation for latency-sensitive flows.
- Private: customer-managed VPC/on-prem option for full control — longer lead time (4–8+ weeks) and procurement work.

Ask from your side for the evaluation sprint:
1) Confirm whether EU-only processing (Frankfurt) is an absolute requirement or if regional routing with EU-first is acceptable.
2) Share two sample prompts / inference profiles and expected RPS for the POC.
3) Quick security checklist below — we can pre-share SOC2 summary and KMS integration notes (attached).

Suggested near-term timeline (example):
- Week 0: Sign MAP and finalize scope (data residency and core endpoints)
- Weeks 1–2: Hosted POC in EU (fastest) + baseline performance metrics
- Weeks 3–4: Dedicated proof (if needed) or opt to proceed to Private onboarding planning
- Week 6–8: Decision point and contractual commitment window

If you'd like, I can loop in our security lead (Irene) and solutions engineer (Ben) this week to triage the SOC/evidence items.

Thanks,
Sofia Ivanova
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
sofia@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0192

Attachments: NimbleOps-MAP-v1.3.pdf, SOC2-Redwood-summary.pdf
From: Daniel Park <daniel@nimbleops.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Sharma <priya@nimbleops.com>, procurement@nimbleops.com
Date: 2027-04-11T14:07:00Z
Subject: Re: Draft MAP: hosting options + timeline (quick read)

Hi Sofia — thanks for the clear summary and the MAP doc. A few quick clarifications from our side: 

- Data residency is firm: all inference and logs for EU customers must remain in EU. Frankfurt-only is ideal. No cross-border replication.
- Our initial RPS profile for the POC: 10 concurrent sessions, burst to 60 reqs/min per endpoint; prompt sizes avg ~500 tokens, with a small subset peaking at 2k tokens.
- Security: we will need SOC2 Type II evidence plus confirmation that KMS/HSM integration can be customer-controlled for key material.

Given the residency requirement, our preference leans to Dedicated or Private. Hosted is only an option if you can guarantee EU-only processing with customer-key control (prefer Dedicated).

Procurement notes: procurement@nimbleops.com — we aim to complete SOW/PO within 6 weeks if the MAP and technical evals go smoothly.

Best,
Daniel Park
Head of Platform Engineering
NimbleOps Inc.

Cc: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-12T08:35:00Z
Subject: Re: Draft MAP: hosting options + timeline (quick read)

Looping in engineering notes and a suggested technical split for the POC: 

Summary of suggested approach (technical):
- Start with Dedicated in Frankfurt as the primary evaluation: gives NimbleOps customer-key control on KMS and avoids cross-border issues. We can provide a dedicated GPU pool in our EU region with isolated tenancy and bring-your-own-keys (BYOK) via our KMS integration.
- Parallel Hosted baseline: spin a small hosted endpoint in EU to get latency and correctness baselines within 48–72 hours. This helps narrow model & quantization choices quickly.
- Private option: we will prepare an onboarding checklist, but expect a 4–8 week integration window (networking, KMS, and airgap if requested).

Tech asks for POC (please provide):
1) Sample prompt set (dev redacted ok).
2) Expected concurrency and largest prompt size (Daniel included above — thanks).
3) Any model family preference (e.g., Llama2-70B vs. Mistral) — if none, we'll propose a default based on latency/cost.

Irene: can you confirm SOC2 artifacts we can share and whether a short KMS integration checklist exists?

Cheers,
Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
ben@redwood.ai
From: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Sofia Ivanova <sofia@redwood.ai>, Daniel Park <daniel@nimbleops.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-15T11:51:00Z
Subject: Re: Draft MAP: hosting options + timeline (quick read)

Hi all — attaching the SOC2 summary and a short KMS integration checklist (see attachment). Quick notes: 

- SOC2: we can share a redacted Type II report under NDA; the SOC2-Redwood-summary.pdf includes control families and the attestation window.
- KMS: Dedicated + Private both support customer-managed keys. Hosted in EU can be configured with customer keys but requires an addendum; we'll surface the SAML/KMS flow in the checklist.
- Evidence turnaround: if NimbleOps executes the standard NDA, we can provide the redacted report within 3 business days.

Proposed next steps (Irene):
1) NimbleOps to sign the mutual NDA (I’ve attached the checklist and will follow up with the security share link).
2) Ben to provision a small Hosted EU endpoint for immediate baseline tests (48–72 hrs).
3) If Dedicated is desired, schedule a technical kickoff to scope networking and KMS BYOK (target next week).

Irene Choi
Security Lead | Redwood Inference
irene@redwood.ai

Attachments referenced: SOC2-Redwood-summary.pdf, KMS-integration-checklist.docx
From: Daniel Park <daniel@nimbleops.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Sharma <priya@nimbleops.com>, procurement@nimbleops.com
Date: 2027-04-18T16:03:00Z
Subject: Re: Draft MAP: hosting options + timeline (quick read)

Thanks — all very helpful.

Quick decision update from our side: we want to proceed with Dedicated in Frankfurt as the primary path and run a parallel Hosted baseline for rapid comparison. We will execute the standard NDA today so Irene can share the Type II report. Procurement will start SOW prep once we have the Dedicated scoping estimate.

Action items we expect from Redwood this week:
- Ben: spin up Hosted EU baseline and share endpoint + sample latency numbers.
- Irene: send redacted SOC2 Type II under NDA and the KMS checklist.
- Sofia: update the MAP to reflect Dedicated as primary path and include a 6-week close window; send updated MAP v1.4.

We’ll aim to have the technical kickoff next Tue (2027-04-20) for Dedicated scoping.

Regards,
Daniel Park
Head of Platform Engineering
NimbleOps Inc.
